in_hebrew.name: תומאס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: תומאס הוא שם עברי שמשמעותו 'תאום' או 'תומך'. השם תומאס מקורו מהמילה הארמית 'תאמה', שפירושה 'תאום'. בתנ'ך, תומאס הוא אחד משנים עשר תלמידיו של ישוע, המכונה 'התאום' (יוחנן 11:16, 20:24). השם תומאס הוא שם נפוץ בקרב יהודים ונוצרים כאחד, ויש לו חשיבות רבה במסורת הנוצרית.

in_greek.name: Θωμάς
in_greek.long_meaning: Θωμάς είναι ένα ελληνικό όνομα που σημαίνει 'δίδυμος' ή 'υποστηρικτής'. Το όνομα Θωμάς προέρχεται από την αραμαϊκή λέξη 'תאמה', που σημαίνει 'δίδυμος'. Στη Βίβλο, ο Θωμάς είναι ένας από τους δώδεκα μαθητές του Ιησού, γνωστός ως 'ο δίδυμος' (Ιωάννης 11:16, 20:24). Το όνομα Θωμάς είναι πολύ συνηθισμένο μεταξύ των Ελλήνων και έχει μεγάλη σημασία στην χριστιανική παράδοση.

in_latin.name: Thomas
in_latin.long_meaning: Thomas is a Latin name that means 'twin' or 'supporter'. The name Thomas originates from the Aramaic word 'taoma', which means 'twin'. In the Bible, Thomas is one of Jesus' twelve apostles, known as 'the twin' (John 11:16, 20:24). The name Thomas has been widely used in Christian tradition and has been popularized by several saints and martyrs throughout history.

in_english.name: Tomas
in_english.long_meaning: The name Tomas, also known as Thomas, originates from the Hebrew-Aramaic word 'Taoma', meaning 'twin' or 'supporter'. data.cultural_impact: Thomas, a name prominent in Christian tradition, carries connections to one of the twelve apostles. This Biblical figure is known for his skepticism towards the resurrection of Jesus, but ultimately his belief was solidified through tangible evidence. This name holds historical and religious significance in the Christian faith, representing the courage to question, seek truth, and follow a belief despite doubt.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, Thomas's journey reflects the complexity of human faith and serves as a reminder of God's ability to turn doubt into strong belief. The name Thomas signifies the enduring strength of faith, as well as the importance of questioning and seeking validation for one's beliefs. Through the strength and commitment demonstrated by Thomas in the face of doubt, this name inspires a deep sense of courage and conviction.

historical_references.reference: Thomas the Apostle, one of the twelve apostles of Jesus Christ, was born in Galilee and was a fisherman by trade. He is best known for his doubt and disbelief in the resurrection of Jesus, as recounted in the Gospel of John. Despite this, he was present at the Last Supper and was with Jesus during the Last Days in Jerusalem. After the death of Jesus, Thomas joined the other apostles in Galilee and was a witness to the risen Christ, who appeared to them. Thomas then spread the word of Christianity in India, where he is believed to have been martyred around AD 72.

Thomas Becket, an English statesman and Archbishop of Canterbury in the late 12th century, is also known as Saint Thomas of Canterbury. He was born into a noble family and studied law in Paris before becoming a monk. He rose through the ranks of the Church, becoming Chancellor of England under King Henry II in 1154. However, their relationship soured when Becket refused to grant Henry the annulment of his marriage to Eleanor of Aquitaine. Becket was subsequently exiled from England and went to France, where he was later appointed Archbishop of Canterbury in 1162. He was martyred in his cathedral in Canterbury in 1170, becoming a symbol of Church independence from secular power and a popular saint in England and Europe.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Tomas is derived from the Aramaic name "Toma," which means "twin." In Christian tradition, it is believed that Thomas was the twin brother of the apostle Doubting Thomas, who was known for his skepticism and required physical proof of Jesus' resurrection before he could believe. Thus, Tomas symbolizes both the duality of human nature and the importance of faith and doubt in the spiritual journey.
